overview: Systems keep arriving from the Pacific through the week. Washington and the Sierra get rain and mountain snow Sunday into Monday, and the Rockies and Northeast see snow and freezing rain before a short dry spell.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A weak system brings light snow to the Cascades Friday, then a brief ridge of high pressure dries things out Saturday. Snow returns Sunday as the next system moves in. Crystal Mountain is the top resort, with 11 inches expected through Monday. The NWS is calling for more, 10 to 23 inches from Friday through Monday night.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Dry, mild weather holds through Saturday. A low Sunday night into Monday brings mostly rain to the valleys and only light snow to the highest peaks. A stronger, colder storm arrives late Monday into Tuesday, with forecasters uncertain how wet it will be. Mammoth expects 11 inches through Tuesday, and the NWS is calling for more, 22 to 37 inches from Sunday night through Tuesday night.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Dry and mild through Saturday, with valley fog in the mornings. An unsettled pattern starts Sunday, with mountain snow above 7,500 feet and gusty southerly winds on the crest. Kirkwood is the top resort, with 11 inches expected through Tuesday. The NWS is calling for more, 20 to 31 inches from Sunday through Tuesday night.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Strong northwest flow brings a Pacific system to western Wyoming and Idaho Friday night through Saturday, with the heaviest snow west of the Divide. Jackson Hole is the top resort, with 10 inches expected through Monday, and a Winter Storm Warning runs Friday into Saturday. The NWS is calling for more, 18 to 37 inches from Friday through Tuesday night.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: A strong storm brings freezing rain to northern New York and Vermont Friday, with icy roads and possible power outages. Light mountain snow follows Saturday. Quebec's Le Massif is the top resort, with 9 inches expected through Monday, and freezing rain warnings run Friday into Saturday.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: A fast-moving system brings strong winds and snow to the northern mountains Friday night into Saturday, making travel hazardous, especially over passes and on I-70. Steamboat is the top resort, with 7 inches expected through Saturday. The NWS is calling for more, 6 to 13 inches from Friday night through Tuesday night, and a Winter Storm Warning runs Friday into Sunday.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Mostly rain at lower elevations with showers and snow mixing in at times. Whistler is the top resort, with 6 inches expected through Monday.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 25, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Dec 6–12. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
